plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES 
Note: All proposals, presentations, and/or documentation to be reviewed and 
discussed at this meeting can be viewed online at the following link: 
https://bit.ly/SalemPACProposals 
Meeting called to order at 6:33pm. 
Roll Call PAC: Jim Bostick (Chair), Becky Fisher, Gwendolyn Rosemond, Brittany Minton, 
Hannah Gathman.  
Absent at Roll Call: Bryan Apito. 
Also Present: Staff: Julie Barry (Senior Planner Arts & Culture); Maura Welch (Clerk). 
• Meeting Minutes Approval - May 19, 2026 and July 21, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
Ms. Barry noted that the June meeting was cancelled and there were no June minutes. The 
May 19 minutes had not been reviewed in July, so both the May 19 and July 21 minutes 
were before the Commission. Members noted minor name and spelling corrections. 
Motion to approve the May 19, 2026 and July 21, 2026 meeting minutes is made by Ms. 
Fisher, seconded by Ms. Rosemond and passes 5-0. 
• FY2027 Budget Planning 
Ms. Barry reviewed the FY2027 draft budget: $25,000 for Public Art, $10,498 for 
Conservation & Maintenance (C&M), and $10,000 for the Downtown Programming Fund. 
The Downtown Programming Fund was reduced by $5,150 for FY2027. 
Several signage costs remain estimates pending final designs and quotes. Ms. Barry expects 
firmer numbers for review in September. 
The Commission revisited additional structural engineering assistance for Roark Congdon's 
400+ Traces of Arrival sculpture. After reviewing the original call and the artist's 
documentation, members agreed not to allocate additional engineering funds and to 
remove that line from the draft budget.

Meeting held remotely via zoom
Because travel costs from Seattle could prevent Mr. Congdon from attending the 
dedication, the Commission agreed instead to add an artist travel stipend: up to $2,000 if 
lodging is included, or $1,500 if lodging is secured separately. Ms. Barry will coordinate the 
details with the artist. 
Ms. Barry estimated that roughly $3,000 would remain in the Public Art fund after the travel 
stipend and the current placeholder for the Rousseau works. 
Members agreed to pause further allocations until September, when signage, travel, and 
Rousseau costs should be clearer. The Public Art & Performance Mini Grant, ArtBox 
continuation, Arts Festival community art sponsorship, and a possible new public art project 
can be revisited then. 
• Artists' Row 2027/2028 Call for Creatives - Recommendations 
Ms. Barry reviewed the Artists' Row application results. Seven reviewers scored applications 
independently and the scores were averaged; some applications were disqualified for 
missing required materials. 
For the Public Artist in Residence (PAiR), Javiera Garcia/Cornucopia Threads received the 
highest score for 2027. Her proposal centers on sculptural textile and fiber work with 
community participation. The next highest-scoring applications were thecollab and Gwyn S 
Marathas. 
The Commission felt thecollab's larger public mural project would benefit from the 
additional planning time available for 2028, with Gwyn S Marathas recommended as 
runner-up. 
Motion is made by Ms. Minton to offer the 2027 PAiR to Javiera Garcia/Cornucopia Threads 
and the 2028 PAiR to thecollab, with Gwyn S Marathas as the 2028 runner-up if thecollab 
declines, seconded by Ms. Fisher and passes 5-0. 
For Studio/Retail/Maker spaces, MiraMar Printmakers received the highest overall score 
and was recommended for Stall #4. North Shore Glass School LLC was recommended to 
remain in Stall #2 for its final eligible cycle. French Press Candle Co. was also discussed for 
Stall #2. 
The Commission discussed Erik Quigley/Death & Decorum and Kimberly Ballou as strong 
candidates to share or divide Stall #1. Members felt their work could complement one 
another. Ms. Barry noted that any taxidermy activity must comply with Artists' Row rules, 
including the prohibition on human remains. 
Leah Tsukamoto/Do-It-Together Salem submitted the only performance-focused 
application. Members discussed the value of performance programming, but noted that the 
application scored lower and focused more on rehearsal and gathering space than public 
performance.
Motion is made by Ms. Gathman to award Stall #4 to MiraMar Printmakers, keep North 
Shore Glass School LLC in Stall #2, and invite Erik Quigley/Death & Decorum and Kimberly 
Ballou to share or divide Stall #1, seconded by Ms. Rosemond and passes 5-0. 
Ms. Barry will contact the selected applicants and discuss a shared or divided Stall #1 with 
Mr. Quigley and Ms. Ballou. If the arrangement is not workable, she will bring the issue back 
to the Commission. 
• Rousseau Collection Donation and Display 
Ms. Barry reviewed the updated Rousseau Collection proposal, draft agreement, and 
possible display locations at Salem High School. The current plan is for two larger paintings 
to enter the City's public art collection, with the remaining materials housed and displayed 
through the high school archive/collection. 
Ms. Barry said elaborate custom cases are not needed at this stage. City-owned works are 
covered by fine art insurance, and Salem High School has existing display cases and 
furniture that may work for smaller materials. 
Ms. Minton supported the high school location because of Rousseau's connection to the 
school and the potential for student research and art education. Members also discussed 
involving students in interpretive materials and displays. 
Ms. Barry recommended property/contact labels on the artworks and language in the 
agreement requiring consultation with the PAC before works are moved. The PAC would 
remain responsible for conservation and maintenance. 
Members were also supportive of exploring a small temporary exhibition of the collection 
before permanent installation, if timing and space allow. 
Because gifts valued over $1,000 require City Council acceptance, Ms. Barry will confirm the 
approval process with the City Clerk and Mayor's Office, obtain a statement of value from 
the estate representative, and finalize the supporting documentation. No formal 
Commission vote was taken. 
• Project & City Updates 
Ms. Barry reported that installation of Roark Congdon's 400+ Traces of Arrival sculpture is 
scheduled for the following week. Base preparation is planned for Monday, with delivery 
and installation on Tuesday. Ms. Barry will document the installation. 
Mr. Congdon declined to design the interpretive sign, so Ms. Barry will move the sign design 
and fabrication forward separately. Final payment will be made after the sculpture is 
installed and accepted. 
MOON Base One has received approval to reopen, with the City hopeful the space will be 
active again early next month. 
Ms. Barry also updated the Commission on Old Town Hall planning. The City is working with 
outside consultants on options that could include an approximately $15 million renovation
and a new community-focused operating model. A fuller report is expected after the 
current phase ends in December. 
Ms. Barry reminded members of upcoming public art and 400+ events, including the early 
September unveiling of the restored George Washington portrait. She is also awaiting Hels 
Gibson's final title-panel design for the Flowers Grow in Massachusetts mural. 
Motion to adjourn is made by Ms. Fisher, seconded by Ms. Gathman and passes 5-0. 
Adjourn - The meeting adjourned at 8:23pm.
